claim: profile.py, the script the doc names as the meter that makes the gate 'a number on that report, not a feeling,' has no bead/goal argument at all — only --session/--days/--since/--until — while the doc defines the gate's unit as 'the goal's output tokens.' A goal that spans more than one orchestrator session (already an established reality in this design elsewhere) cannot be measured as one number: --session undercounts by excluding the goal's other sessions (false PASS on partial data), and --days/--since overcounts by co-mingling unrelated concurrent goals.

claim: The doctrine's existing durable, population-level verdict register (execute-plan.md's `_interspect_insert_evidence` call, feeding interspect calibration) is the counter-assay mechanism this lens's parent-1 finding says the design lacks, but Pattern F's dispatch shape never states whether it routes through that call site, and even where reached the write is fail-open at every layer and its schema (a bare `pass` boolean, `escalation_count` hardcoded to 0) cannot distinguish a validator's independent re-verification from a mechanical replay of the executor's own checker.
intersection_justification: Distsys half: a durable log exists but is call-site-bound to execute-plan.md's checkpoint-gated completion block and fails open/silently at three separate layers — invisible without tracing the shell script and its DB-existence check. Assay half: even a successful write is diagnostically inert for Q-A because its schema conflates two assay strengths (replay vs. independent confirmation) under one boolean — invisible without the independence framing. Neither parent alone reaches 'wire it up AND redesign the schema's independence field before pilots start.'
evidence: execute-plan.md:44-52 wraps `_interspect_insert_evidence` in `2>/dev/null || true` and a `[[ -n "$interspect_root" ]]` guard, and hardcodes `escalation_count:0`; lib-interspect.sh:3047-3048 has `[[ -f "$db" ]] || return 1` (silent no-op absent the DB); execute-plan.md:9 mandates checkpoint pauses ('never auto-approve') that sit in tension with Pattern F's thin, autonomous orchestrator (design doc lines 12-19), which never names its own dispatch/recording path.

claim: 'Frozen criteria' freezes text, not repo state (model-routing.md:102), and Pattern F touches a shared, unpinned trunk at three separate temporal points (authoring/gauge-lint, executor dispatch, validator re-run) with no version pin or lease named at any of them; Q-E scopes plan drift to the executor only, missing that the validator's later re-verification can drift again after the executor's own pass, and the only coordination fix (pin the commit) collapses the validator's re-run into a guaranteed-identical replay — reinforcing, not resolving, the parent-1 replay finding.
intersection_justification: Distsys half: three separate spawns touch a shared, unpinned trunk with no pin/lease named and no strike-taxonomy category for the resulting spurious FAIL — a pure assay reviewer would assume 'frozen criteria' already covers reproducibility. Assay half: the obvious coordination fix (pin the commit) is not free — it collapses the validator's re-run into the exact guaranteed-replay condition the parent-1 finding says certifies nothing — a pure distsys reviewer would recommend the pin without noticing it fully realizes the other failure mode. Only tracing both together shows the design is silently choosing between two failure modes rather than missing an obvious fix.
evidence: design doc:34 (Q-E) scopes drift to 'a fresh executor cannot notice'; model-routing.md:102 says only 'criteria frozen before execution' (content freeze, no state pin); model-routing.md:114-119 shows gauge-lint runs against the plan's emitted output at authoring time, a third unpinned temporal snapshot; model-routing.md:110-113's strike taxonomy excludes sandbox denials/auth expiry/infra errors as non-strikes but names no category for trunk drift between spawns, so a drift-induced FAIL silently consumes strike budget identically to a genuine defect.
